transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I guess… people at work have been saying I’m hard to follow. Like when I’m trying to explain inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, my words kind of jump around — trucks, Thursdays, the church grill, my boss’s tone… and then everyone just looks at me like they don’t know what I’m talking about.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed a period where your mood felt unusually high, energetic, or irritable, along with needing much less sleep than usual?
I don’t think so. I mean… I haven’t felt unusually up or anything like that. Sleep’s been… I don’t know, not something I’ve really tracked.
How long have you been noticing this pattern of your thoughts and words jumping around when you try to explain things?
Maybe… around six months. That’s when people started really noticing it at work, the way I’d explain things or just stop on the floor. Hard to say exactly.
During these past six months, have you also experienced stretches where you felt persistently sad, hopeless, or lost interest and pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
I’m not sure. I mean… I wouldn’t say I’ve been hopeless. Maybe quieter than usual, but I haven’t really thought about it like that. I don’t know about “persistently,” no.
Have you noticed anything unusual, like hearing voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, or having beliefs that others find hard to accept?
I’m not sure. I don’t really… I haven’t noticed voices like that, no. As for beliefs, I mean, people don’t always understand what I’m trying to say, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean.
Over these past six months, has this difficulty with your thoughts and speech been present continuously, or have there been times when it went away completely and you felt back to your normal self?

It hasn’t really gone away, no. It’s been… kind of there, on and off maybe, but the jumbled explaining and stopping at work has been noticeable for about six months. I don’t think I’ve felt completely back to normal in that way.

Over these past six months, have you noticed yourself pulling away from friends or family, losing interest in activities you used to care about, or feeling like your emotions or facial expressions have become more flat or muted?

I don’t know… maybe I’ve been keeping to myself a bit more, but I haven’t really thought of it that way. I still talk to people when I need to. As far as my face or emotions being flat, I’m not sure. No one’s really said that to me.

Have coworkers or family noticed you doing things that seemed unusual or out of place for the situation—like odd behavior on the job, unpredictable actions, or trouble completing tasks in the expected way?

Yeah… I guess some people have noticed. At work, sometimes I’ll just be on the sales floor pacing the same aisle, fixing the same batteries again and again. Or I’ll be standing there with the schedule clipboard, and the associates are waiting on me to tell them what to do, and I just… don’t get to it right away.
Over these past six months, would you say your ability to keep up with your usual responsibilities at work or in your personal life has been significantly affected because of these difficulties?

Yeah… it has affected things. At work they don’t really trust me to run the busy weekend shifts anymore. After my last review, my boss said if I don’t get it together, I could be suspended.

And at home… my wife’s had to take over some things I used to handle. People get… uncomfortable or confused around me, I guess. So she steps in.
Have you been using any alcohol, recreational drugs, or new medications, or been diagnosed with any medical or neurological conditions during this six-month period?
Not really sure what you’re looking for. I mean… nothing new that I can think of. I haven’t been told I have some condition or anything.

Yeah… I guess it didn’t just start all at once. It’s been building maybe… around eleven months now. Since the new district manager came in and started pushing harder on forecasts and schedules. Things started feeling off then, before it got this bad.

I don’t know. I mean… I haven’t caught anyone doing that exactly. Things at work have been tense, but I can’t really say they’re all working against me or anything.
Over these past several months, have you found it harder to start or follow through on tasks—at work or at home—even simple ones, because you just don't feel motivated or driven to begin them?
I’m not sure. I mean, I have days where I put things off, but I don’t know if it’s more than usual. I still get things done, mostly.

When you find yourself pacing the same aisle or checking the same batteries over and over, do you feel like you're doing it without any clear purpose or reason, almost like you can't help it, even though it doesn't help you finish your work?

Yeah… sometimes. I’ll realize I’ve been in the same aisle for a while, straightening the same batteries, and it’s not really helping anything. Or I’m just standing there with the schedule clipboard while people are waiting on me. I don’t know why I get stuck like that.
